messages:
maya: Heads-up — I ran a set of multiplexed co-residency experiments on prod-like hw (A100 80GB) to test a new 'vram scheduler' we sketched last week. Observed an unexpected perf regression and a couple OOMs when the KV cache warms.

luke: short summary numbers? p50/p95/cost?

maya: quick numbers: single-model baseline (Llama-70B quant) p50=85ms. With co-residency + scheduler p50 -> 120ms, p95 320ms -> 480ms. Throughput per-GPU down ~18%. GPU memory steady ~62GB but transient spikes to 78GB during KV cache refill.

rashmi: did the scheduler change workspace sizing or allocation policy? sounds like transient spikes from cache refill.

maya: yes — scheduler switches active model partitions and gives each model a configurable workspace target instead of absolute allocation. Implementation used timed reclaim + lazy compaction. Snippet of the allocator hook we used:

```
// simplified
void schedule_swap(ModelA, ModelB) {
  set_workspace_target(ModelA, 0.65 * partition_size);
  set_workspace_target(ModelB, 0.35 * partition_size);
  start_lazy_compaction(timeout_ms=200);
}
```

maya: profiler (ncu-like) shows GC/compaction kicks off, but kernel selection falls back to slower kernels during compaction window which increases peak temporary buffers. Example stack during spike:

```
alloc_large_temp(24MB) -> nvrtc_fallback_kernel -> cuBLAS_gemm_alternative -> allocate_kv_temp(90MB)
```

jordan: nvrtc_fallback_kernel is suspicious — that usually indicates our fused ops didn't match heuristics and we fell back to JIT'd kernels with higher scratch. Repro on quant and fp16 builds?

maya: repro'd on both. fp16 less bad (~12% throughput loss), quantized run shows more fragmentation.

vik: can you paste allocator fragmentation / free-list stats around the spike?

maya: snapshot before spike:

```
total_allocated: 62.1GB
free_fragments: 128
largest_free: 3.2GB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.12
```

During spike:

```
total_allocated: 78.6GB
free_fragments: 342
largest_free: 1.1GB
fragmentation_ratio: 0.42
oom_events: 2 (kv-refill, swap)
```

rashmi: frag_ratio 0.42 explains inability to satisfy a 16GB contiguous temp allocation causing fallback/oom. Two ideas:
- add transient reservation (prefetch buffer) per-partition to handle KV refill bursts
- change compaction from lazy to synchronous when refill expected

luke: also check batching heuristics — are concurrent small requests still getting fused? If compaction shifts timing, batching windows might shrink and cause more kernel launches (and scratch allocations).

maya: instrumented batching windows: with scheduler enabled avg batch size dropped 9% during partition reassignments because requests routed to 'warming' partition which enforces conservative batching until KV steady-state.

jordan: routing should be aware of KV-shipping state. Tag partitions with 'warmness' metric and avoid full-pop routing until kv_cache_fill < threshold. That avoids simultaneous refill across co-resident models.

vik: other mitigation: per-model ephemeral slack buffer (reserve 2-4GB) that allocator treats as pre-committed for temp spikes. On allocation failure, trigger swap-out of least-recently-touched model segments instead of global OOM.

maya: prototyped ephemeral slack: reserve 3GB per partition, allocator marks those pages as 'evictable'. Result: no OOMs in 20 runs, p95 improved to 360ms (from 480ms), but steady memory usage +6% which reduces peak host density.

luke: trade-off reasonable for Dedicated customers. For Hosted, make it adaptive: slack grows on prediction of incoming KV refill (based on request pattern).

rashmi: can we compact KV cache layout to avoid large contiguous allocations? E.g., split big KV blobs into smaller shards placed across fragments to reduce contiguous alloc pressure.

maya: explored sharding: helps but increases lookup overhead (+2-3% CPU) and slight latency tail for large contexts. Compaction cost shifts to pointer mgmt.

jordan: kernel selection side — if fallback to nvrtc causes larger scratch, prefer compiled fused kernels with preallocated scratch or maintain small pool of compiled kernels per-arch to avoid JIT hits during critical windows.

maya: saw JIT-only kernels appear when seq-len distribution changed and kernel cache eviction had removed compiled variants. Fix: increase kernel cache capacity and pin hot kernels during partition transitions.

vik: action items proposal:
1) implement ephemeral slack reservation (configurable per-tier) — short-term mitigation
2) add 'warmness' tag + routing guard to reduce simultaneous KV refills
3) increase kernel cache pinning during swap/compaction windows
4) evaluate shard-KV vs monolithic-KV for fragmentation trade-offs

luke: +1. Also add perf test that simulates N-model co-residency with staggered arrivals to ensure we don't regress tail.

maya: I'll open a PR with slack reserve prototype and perf harness results. Attaching run id and perf-bot trace: perf-bot:perf/1772345678/multiplexed-run-42

perf-bot: Trace attached: https://perf.internal/runs/1772345678

oncall-bot: Alert suppressed. Noted 2 OOM events; no customer impact recorded.

jordan: Maya, include unit test that forces nvrtc fallback to ensure kernel cache pinning prevents the scratch spike.

maya: will do. Landing prototype behind feature flag and running 48h soak on dedicated pool.

vik: thanks Maya — please cc infra and SRE when you start soak so we can watch allocator/oom metrics.

maya: will do. Thanks all :thumbsup:
